guides.favoredWhen: Darius wins by staying healthy into early magic resist and pulling after blind is down; Teemo wins if he keeps Darius chipped below the all-in threshold and seeds every approach with shrooms.

keyTips.text: Never fight him while low. He wins the melee if Darius starts below roughly 90% health, so concede last-hits until Second Wind tops Darius back up rather than forcing a bad trade.
keyTips.heading: Health gate

keyTips.text: Buy Negatron Cloak and Mercury's Treads before walking up. His poke only matters while Darius lacks magic resist, and Treads cut the slow that lets him run Darius down after a short trade.
keyTips.heading: First buys

keyTips.text: Hold Apprehend until he steps past the minion line. He wants to poke from beyond pull range and disengage with his W movespeed into seeded shrooms, so a wasted pull leaves Darius blinded in the open with nothing to show for it.
keyTips.heading: Pull discipline

tips.text: Check the turret-side bush before leashing or walking to lane at level 1. His standard cheese is waiting there for a free blind-plus-autos opener that ruins the health gate for the whole lane.
tips.heading: Level 1

tips.text: After a pull lands, expect blind plus a step inside Q. Open with W crippling immediately after Apprehend lands, so he cannot walk into the Q dead zone for free while Darius is blinded.
tips.heading: Pull answer

tips.text: Do not rely on a single slow to stick to him. He commonly runs Swifties precisely to blunt Decimate slows, so plan the all-in around the Stridebreaker active rather than a foot chase.
tips.heading: Stick tools

tips.text: Make him spend his burst movespeed before Apprehend. Whether it is his W sprint or a rune proc, the pull only sticks once that speed is gone, and Stridebreaker's slow creates a far more reliable window than a raw walk-up.
tips.heading: Movespeed first

tips.text: Take only short W-plus-Q contacts while his blind is up. His whole counter is blind-then-run into shrooms, so deal damage in brief Crippling-plus-Decimate touches and reset instead of chasing through the blind.
tips.heading: Short contacts

tips.text: Sweep with a red trinket after level 6 and never walk a shroomed choke at low stacks. His shrooms decide where fights happen, and one blind walk through them turns a won side lane into a throw.
tips.heading: Shroom sweep

tips.text: Prefer side pressure when his shroom coverage makes grouped routes unsafe. He cannot cover every lane entrance at once, so push the side he has not seeded and force him to answer without his minefield.
tips.heading: Side-lane plan

itemization.text: Take Conqueror with Second Wind, opening Doran's Shield into Negatron Cloak and Mercury's Treads, then Stridebreaker and Kaenic Rookern as the core package that lets Darius walk up at all.
Finish Kaenic Rookern once teamfights start. The shield plus magic resist keeps a stray shroom or blind-plus-focus from ending Darius before the frontline fight begins.

guides.favoredWhen: Darius wins by spacing at W edge, interrupting Counter Strike, and Ghosting only after E ends; Jax wins short trades where he blocks Crippling Strike and stacks Hemorrhage freely.

keyTips.text: Never open with Apprehend and refuse short trades. Space at W outer edge, beyond his W range, and let him come to you instead of offering the brawl he wants.
keyTips.heading: Spacing rule

keyTips.text: Reserve Apprehend to interrupt Counter Strike or his leap. Holding E keeps his stun honest; spending it first gives him a free engage with no answer ready.
keyTips.heading: Hold E

keyTips.text: Let Counter Strike finish before Ghosting. Chasing into an active E wastes the summoner, so start the run-down at E expiry and build to five stacks into the ultimate at Spear of Shojin.
keyTips.heading: Ghost timing

tips.text: Punish from Q edge without committing. He closes only when E is ready to block the W answer, so meet each approach with Q and step out instead of trading inside his stun.
tips.heading: Q edge

tips.text: Respect his Ignite window. He takes Ignite to limit your Decimate healing, so refuse committed all-ins while it is up and fight once it is down.
tips.heading: Ignite respect

tips.text: Predict the E reactivation and time W to land as the dodge ends. Watch his rhythm across trades: the W that lands right after Counter Strike expires is what turns the exchange.
tips.heading: Beat the dodge

tips.text: Answer his leap-disjoint with Q plus Flash. When he times the leap to avoid Decimate, add Flash to the Q cast so the heal and stacks still land.
tips.heading: Q Flash

tips.text: Ghost only after E ends and keep the chase in open ground. His plan is to block W and reset the ring, so do not start the run-down until the stun threat is gone.
tips.heading: Run-down

tips.text: Prefer side lanes over teamfighting into his E. A side lane gives room to space his autos and stack to five, while a grouped fight lets him stun you inside his team.
tips.heading: Side-lane plan

itemization.text: Take Conqueror with Transcendence, opening Doran's Blade through Ruby Crystals into Boots, then Spear of Shojin into Stridebreaker and Sterak's Gage for the stack-and-chase package.

guides.favoredWhen: Darius wins by denying level 1, dodging the stun, and converting the Bramble-Shojin side-lane plan; Irelia wins level 4–5 punishes and the Blade of the Ruined King turn.

keyTips.text: Deny her XP at level 1 before her passive stacks. Stand between her and the wave early; an unstacked Irelia cannot contest your zone.
keyTips.heading: Level-1 deny

keyTips.text: Dodge her E and never chase through minions. Sidestep the stun line instead of walking it straight, and let chained Q dashes expire without an answer.
keyTips.heading: Stun discipline

keyTips.text: Rush Bramble Vest plus Plated Steelcaps before her Blade of the Ruined King. That window answers her rush; without it, her completed item turns every all-in.
keyTips.heading: Armor timing

tips.text: Give her no punish window at levels 4–5. She starts winning fights there off your missed Qs, so cast Q only when she cannot answer and concede the brief peak instead of forcing into it.
tips.heading: Respect the peak

tips.text: Hold Q edge while she repositions. Each dash is a guess at your cast point, so delay Q until she commits to a minion rather than throwing it at her first dash.
tips.heading: Delayed Q

tips.text: Never walk into her R after level 6. The slow sets up her stun, so step out of the blades and re-engage only once the slow field expires.
tips.heading: Post-6 respect

tips.text: Answer Blade of the Ruined King with short trades. Each missed dodge costs more once her item is done, so freeze and punish cooldowns instead of brawling.
tips.heading: Post-item rule

tips.text: Stack to five and ult once Spear of Shojin is done. After that spike your stacked trades outscale her burst, so build patiently and finish with the reset.
tips.heading: Shojin turn

tips.text: Prefer side lanes over grouped fights. A side lane gives room to space her dashes and stack freely, while a grouped fight lets her chain Q through your team onto you.
tips.heading: Side-lane plan

itemization.text: Open Doran's Blade into Bramble Vest and Plated Steelcaps against her rush, then Stridebreaker into Spear of Shojin and Sterak's Gage.

guides.favoredWhen: Darius wins by pressing early, baiting W, and finishing before the realm; Mordekaiser wins if he reaches Rylai's even and opens the duel with his ult.

keyTips.text: Start fighting at level 2 or 3, never the level-1 coinflip. His early pattern is readable once abilities are down; level 1 is the only window where variance beats you.
keyTips.heading: Opening level

keyTips.text: Pull then ult before his W comes up. If he holds W for your R, bait it first: E into R denies him the block window entirely.
keyTips.heading: Beat the shield

keyTips.text: Win the item race to Shojin before his Rylai's. At even farm he spikes first on the cheaper item, so the lane is a clock you must beat.
keyTips.heading: Item clock

tips.text: Press the first three minutes while he concedes. Take free health with Q edge and zone him off last-hits instead of handing him uncontested farm.
tips.heading: Early press

tips.text: Ghost-dodge his Q and E rather than eating chains. Save Ghost for his pull combo, and step out of every Q cone instead of trading inside it.
tips.heading: Dodge pattern

tips.text: Respect his level 4–5 Ignite all-in when healthy. Track Ignite before committing; if it is up and he is full, refuse the extended fight.
tips.heading: Ignite respect

tips.text: Avoid his Qs once Rylai's lands. The slow field makes every later Q stick, so stop standing in pull range at even items.
tips.heading: Post-spike rule

tips.text: Reach five stacks and ult before he realms you. His stat steal guts your damage inside the realm, so finish the setup outside it.
tips.heading: Pre-realm finish

tips.text: If he realms someone else, punish immediately. A quick combo into R, even before five stacks, turns his engage into your reset opening.
tips.heading: Teamfight punish

itemization.text: Open Doran's Shield into Pickaxe and Boots, then Spear of Shojin, Boots of Swiftness, Stridebreaker, and Kaenic Rookern for the stack-and-chase package.

guides.favoredWhen: Darius wins short trades and E-pulls on her dashes while tracking stacks; Akali wins if she drops stacks in shroud and all-ins a chunked target.

keyTips.text: Take short auto plus W plus Q trades, then disengage before Titanic Hydra. The burst-and-out pattern denies her extended combo while your item turn approaches.
keyTips.heading: Trade pattern

keyTips.text: Pull her E-dash and never throw E into shroud. Her dash commits her to a line; your pull answers it, while shroud eats blind casts.
keyTips.heading: E discipline

keyTips.text: Track three stacks: she shrouds to drop them. Re-engage as the shroud fades instead of letting the reset go free.
keyTips.heading: Stack tracking

tips.text: When she steps inside your Q, answer with W and autos. She enters the ring to deny the edge and heal, so punish the entry instead of chasing the whiffed cast.
tips.heading: Inner-ring answer

tips.text: Punish her Q and E cooldowns with short trades. Step in while either is down and leave before the full sequence returns.
tips.heading: Cooldown abuse

tips.text: Finish Negatron into Titanic for the repeatable three-stack trade. The auto reset lands stacks even through shroud, so the trade no longer needs vision.
tips.heading: Item turn

tips.text: Disengage with Stormraider speed after trades. Take the burst and leave before her return combo, resetting on your terms.
tips.heading: Trade exits

tips.text: Press side-lane towers instead of hunting teamfight catches. You rarely catch her grouped without assured resets, so convert pressure where she must answer.
tips.heading: Side-lane plan

tips.text: Reset when chunked. Her all-in line on a low target is real, so only commit above it and give the freeze rather than the kill.
tips.heading: Health discipline

itemization.text: Open Doran's Shield into Giant's Belt and Negatron Cloak, then Titanic Hydra, Boots of Swiftness, Kaenic Rookern, and Hullbreaker for the trade-and-shove package.

guides.favoredWhen: Darius wins by freezing the wave and sticking to Garen after Stridebreaker while tracking execute thresholds; Garen wins short E-auto-Q bursts and level-6 executes.

keyTips.text: Cheater-recall on wave 3 or 4 for Cull, then freeze on your side. The frozen wave forces him to overextend into pull range or concede farm.
keyTips.heading: Freeze plan

keyTips.text: Trade less before Stridebreaker, then stick with its slow. The item is the lane's hinge: before it, concede the mobility game; after it, he cannot walk away from stacked trades.
keyTips.heading: Stridebreaker hinge

keyTips.text: Manage Bone Plating around his burst windows. When Plating is down at levels 1–2, refuse his E-auto-Q; with Plating up, you can contest the same trade.
keyTips.heading: Plating windows

tips.text: Punish his attempts to break the freeze. If he walks up to crash the frozen wave, meet him with the pull rather than letting him reset for free.
tips.heading: Punish breaks

tips.text: Do not walk into the lane brush at level 1. Meet the wave instead, take short contact, and back out before he can extend an auto-Q-auto into a longer duel.
tips.heading: Level 1

tips.text: Follow his speed rune with your own and rotate first. Clear side waves quickly and move, since he covers the map faster later and punishes late rotations.
tips.heading: Rotation race

tips.text: Run him down the long lane when the wave sits on your side. With Ghost up and distance behind him, his short-trade pattern cannot save him; without Ghost, hold the freeze instead of diving.
tips.heading: Long-lane chase

tips.text: Respect the level-6 execute range. Around 65% health with his Ignite up and no pull available, his full burst can finish you; reset or hold summoners before crossing that line.
tips.heading: Execute respect

tips.text: At rank-3 ultimate, stay above his execute threshold and follow an ally's engage. Enter after the fight starts rather than opening it, so his burst lands on someone else first.
tips.heading: Teamfight entry

itemization.text: Take Stormraider's Surge with Cash Back and the movement-speed shard, opening Doran's Blade into Cull and Boots of Swiftness, then Stridebreaker, Spear of Shojin, and Sterak's Gage.

guides.favoredWhen: Darius wins by spacing at Q edge and converting Shojin stacks; Volibear wins level-3 sustained trades and R-timed engages.

keyTips.text: Respect levels 1–2 and the bleed stacks. He fears your early zone, so press with spacing but never donate the all-in he wants.
keyTips.heading: Early respect

keyTips.text: Pull and trade at Q edge; never stand and brawl to the death. His Lethal Tempo wins static slugfests, so Q and step out instead of trading inside his autos.
keyTips.heading: Edge trading

keyTips.text: Build five stacks and spend R once Shojin completes. The stacked reset is your kill condition, so stack patiently and finish with the dunk.
keyTips.heading: Shojin turn

tips.text: Punish level 1 without overextending the deny. Take the free health and zone, but do not chase past the wave for XP he will reclaim anyway.
tips.heading: Level-1 punish

tips.text: When he steps inside Q, W him instead of whiffing the edge. The inner-ring entry denies your heal, so answer with the slow and autos.
tips.heading: Inner answer

tips.text: Respect level 3. His Q plus marked-W sustained trade is his strongest window, so refuse extended contact until your item answer lands.
tips.heading: Level-3 respect

tips.text: Vary pull timing because he times R against it. Never pull on pattern; hold E until his R answer cannot cover the cast.
tips.heading: Pull discipline

tips.text: Race Shojin plus Stridebreaker into his Rod plus Navori two items. Your spike beats his at even farm, so force the issue in that window.
tips.heading: Spike race

tips.text: Take teamfights from strength. If he catches up to full build his value rises, so convert your mid-game edge before parity returns.
tips.heading: Teamfight timing

itemization.text: Take Conqueror with Transcendence and Axiom Arcanist, opening Doran's Blade into Mercury's Treads and Shojin, with Executioner's Calling, Stridebreaker, and Sterak's Gage.

guides.favoredWhen: Darius wins by baiting Riposte, spacing vitals, and pressing the pre-first-item window; Fiora wins the post-item side-lane if Riposte answers the pull.

keyTips.text: Vary pull and ult timing to bait Riposte. Never give her a predictable E: threaten, hold, and cast only when the parry guesses wrong.
keyTips.heading: Bait the parry

keyTips.text: After she Qs in, answer W plus Q. The contact either forces her parry early or loses her the trade on the spot.
keyTips.heading: Answer the dash

keyTips.text: Zone her off the wave at levels 1–2. She concedes everything before level 3, so take the farm gap while it is free.
keyTips.heading: Early zone

tips.text: Do not chase her max-range Q pokes at level 1. Let the unanswerable pokes expire and hold position instead of donating health for nothing.
tips.heading: Poke patience

tips.text: Commit only after she dashes in. Her mobility dodges dry Qs, so trade on her entry rather than throwing Qs at her spacing.
tips.heading: No dry Qs

tips.text: Time Stridebreaker against her Q dash. Active as she commits so the slow tracks her, then hold Q edge while it lasts.
tips.heading: Stridebreaker tracking

tips.text: Press before her first item lands. Her reliable edge arrives with it against a careful pilot, so force the lane while she is still item-gated.
tips.heading: Pre-item window

tips.text: Wall her ultimate. Stand with a wall at your back so one vital stays denied and her full proc plus healing zone never completes.
tips.heading: Beat the duel

tips.text: Take side lanes only with spacing and items. After three or four items your spaced 1v1 holds, but a chaotic grouped fight lets her reach all four vitals.
tips.heading: Side-lane rule

tips.text: Hold Ghost as the answer to her disengage. She fears the held summoner more than the spent one, so threaten with it and cast only once she commits.
tips.heading: Ghost threat

itemization.text: Open Doran's Shield into Bramble Vest or Executioner's Calling and Plated Steelcaps, then Stridebreaker, Spear of Shojin, and Sterak's Gage.

guides.favoredWhen: Darius wins by holding E for Hookshot and spacing her true-damage Q; Camille wins if she baits the pull and dodges Q with her ultimate.

keyTips.text: Save Apprehend to interrupt Hookshot and never spend it first. Holding E keeps her engage honest; spending it gives her a free dash with no answer ready.
keyTips.heading: Hold E

keyTips.text: Never initiate with E. Her ultimate dodges your Q and traps you for the gank, so let her commit before answering.
keyTips.heading: No blind pulls

keyTips.text: Keep trades short. Her plan is Q damage then E away, so answer at Q edge and refuse the chase she wants.
keyTips.heading: Trade length

tips.text: Respect level 1 if she holds Flash plus Ignite with Q. Concede the cheese angle rather than donating first blood to the burst window.
tips.heading: Level-1 respect

tips.text: Freeze and make her choose. A frozen wave forces her to pick farm or roam, so hold it and ping every departure.
tips.heading: Freeze plan

tips.text: Space her true-damage second Q. Never stand at its edge for free; step out of the empowered cast and re-engage after it lands.
tips.heading: Dodge Q2

tips.text: When she steps inside your Q, hold the cast and W her instead. She enters the inner ring to deny the edge, so punish the entry with the slow rather than whiffing.
tips.heading: Inner-ring answer

tips.text: Punish her backline dives after R. Once the ultimate is down, turn on her team fight instead of letting her reset onto a carry.
tips.heading: Dive punish

tips.text: Ghost only when her R and E are down. She saves the ultimate to dodge and avoids Ghost chases, so start the run-down once both mobility tools are spent.
tips.heading: Ghost timing

itemization.text: Open Doran's Blade through Cloth Armor and Phage into Plated Steelcaps, then Stridebreaker, Spear of Shojin, and Sterak's Gage.

guides.favoredWhen: Darius wins by spacing Q, forcing E defensively, and finishing at Shojin stacks; Aatrox wins full combos and level-6 bursts.

keyTips.text: Space around Q and never eat his full combo. Give ground during each cast sequence and step back in only once the blades land.
keyTips.heading: Spacing rule

keyTips.text: Take short E plus auto plus W plus Q trades once Executioner's Calling lands. His sustain is mostly combat healing, so the anti-heal window is when your trade wins.
keyTips.heading: Anti-heal window

keyTips.text: Press level 1 and threaten Ghost. He respects both, so contest the opening wave instead of conceding it for free.
keyTips.heading: Level-1 press

tips.text: Never dash forward into his pull range blindly. He holds E for your step-in, so approach on foot and force him to spend Qs defensively.
tips.heading: Patient approach

tips.text: Do not time your pull on his second Q. His E repositions mid-sequence and evades exactly that timing, so hold E until the dash is spent.
tips.heading: Hold pull

tips.text: Respect the level-6 burst, especially with Ignite. His all-in turn arrives with R, so track both summoner and ultimate before trading below full health.
tips.heading: Burst respect

tips.text: Slow him with Stridebreaker to force E defensively. Once the slow sticks, his reposition goes to survival instead of combos, and your window opens.
tips.heading: Stridebreaker use

tips.text: Build five stacks and finish with R once Shojin completes. After that spike your stacked trades outscale his healing, so stack patiently and close with the reset.
tips.heading: Shojin turn

tips.text: Favor side lanes over grouped fights. The 1v1 lets you control spacing and stacks, while a grouped fight gives him multi-target combo angles.
tips.heading: Side-lane plan

itemization.text: Take Conqueror with Celerity, opening Doran's Blade into Plated Steelcaps and Executioner's Calling, then Stridebreaker and Spear of Shojin.

guides.favoredWhen: Darius wins by spacing at W range and timing the ultimate after Sett spends Haymaker; Sett wins full-health brawls where his pull lands into the true-damage W.

keyTips.text: Never trade at his auto range. Open with W into Q from your longer W reach, so he must spend his pull to answer or concede the poke exchange.
keyTips.heading: Spacing opener

keyTips.text: Build two passive stacks before he reaches auto range. Once both sides finish Stridebreaker, spacing and active timing decide the duel, so enter it stacked, not flat.
keyTips.heading: Stack first

keyTips.text: Never spend the ultimate into a held Haymaker. Sett players chip you first and time W for your ult, so bait it out with Q and W trades and only commit R after W is gone.
keyTips.heading: Ult timing

tips.text: Levels 1–3, position outside his auto range and let W plus Q do the work. Each cast forces a choice on him: spend his pull early or take free damage.
Once his pull is down, he has no clean way to start an all-in. Hold your pull for his re-engage and keep the trade at Q edge instead of walking into his autos.
tips.heading: Punish the spent pull

tips.text: Reach five Hemorrhage stacks through short W and Q contacts before committing. His side wants to chip you and answer the all-in, so do not extend a flat fight at full health into his second rotation.
tips.heading: Stack discipline

tips.text: Time your Stridebreaker active against his. With the item done on both sides, the duel turns on who slows whom first: active as he steps in, then stay at Q edge while it lasts.
tips.heading: Stridebreaker timing

tips.text: Keep his pull from starting a clean all-in. When he drags you in, space back toward Q edge instead of standing still and brawling at his auto range.
tips.heading: Deny the engage

tips.text: Dodge the true-damage part of Haymaker ({cd:875:W}). Never stand still directly in front of him while W is available; move out before it fires, then re-engage while it is down.
tips.heading: Beat Haymaker

tips.text: Prefer side-lane pressure over grouped fights. His ultimate can isolate you in front of his team, while a side lane gives you room to space his pull and chase him down once it is down.
tips.heading: Side-lane plan

itemization.text: Take Conqueror with Bone Plating and Overgrowth, opening Doran's Blade into Plated Steelcaps, then Stridebreaker and Sterak's Gage as the core duel package.
If he rushes Blade of the Ruined King, start Bramble Vest and finish Thornmail before Sterak's, so his extended trades stop outpacing your stacks.

sources.author: Autolykus
sources.rankClaim: Grandmaster (profile badge; title claims Challenger) · Sett main

keyTips.text: Reach level 3 before the first gank, since all three basics must be online to engage well.
Spike hard at level 6, when R adds an execute threat to duels and skirmishes.
Peel in teamfights and hit the closest enemy instead of diving the backline alone.

tips.text: After level 3, path to pushed lanes around enemy vision so targets get less warning.
Counter-gank whenever possible and turn the enemy arrival into a winning skirmish.
Check enemy inventories for early Grievous Wounds before dueling, and refuse commits into a buyer.
Treat the first finished component as a trading spike, contesting most junglers only when matchup and health allow.
At level 9, press maxed Q for stronger damage and all-in threat.
At level 11, use the second R point as another damage spike for fights and picks.
Without a forming fight, push a side lane and duel the defender when the 1v1 favors Darius.
Time R as the execute to secure the takedown and carry its reset onto the next target.
After a couple of items, blend meaningful damage with enough durability to stay in fights.
Build the lead through ganks, counter-ganks, and favorable duels off the early level and item spikes.
Stay with teammates in fights and chain R takedowns into reset kills.
Flank only on routes that still rejoin the team fight promptly.
Hold near the team at neutral objectives; threaten the backline while ahead, or peel with E for allies while behind.
Convert the early and mid advantage fast, since Darius fades late as opponents stack items and durability.

keyTips.text: Press early lane strength for gold and kill pressure from the first waves.
Bend the wave into a freeze or slow push so opponents must walk into Ghost or gank threat.
Stack the passive to five on a reachable target, then execute with R and turn onto the rest of the fight.

tips.text: Grow the slow push large; the stacked wave deters ganks and helps turn a 1v2 through passive bonus damage.
Poke with Q while freezing, aiming to miss minions so the freeze survives.
Save Ghost whenever possible and spend it on real all-ins rather than every trade.
Walk or Ghost up to stack the passive, holding E until the target burns their escape.
Start with E only when the pull makes a true all-in; otherwise keep it for escaping targets.
Sit in the side lane while major summoners stay down, since Darius barely moves without them.
Keep side pressure rolling to grow the experience and gold lead.
Steal nearby enemy camps when their top laner leaves and the jungler works the opposite side.
Join objective fights only after shoving the side wave, forcing an answer during the setup.
Group around imminent objectives and farm the side lane while nothing brews.
Let the fight develop while stacking, then commit deeper the moment the five-stack threshold lands.
Keep side farm and level edges high so fights start with an item and experience advantage.

itemization.text: Run Conqueror with Triumph, Legend: Alacrity, and Last Stand, plus Bone Plating and Overgrowth, for extended fights.
Open Doran's Blade into all-in lanes and Doran's Shield into short-trade or poke lanes.
Rush Stridebreaker, with Trinity Force as the alternative.
Build Plated Steelcaps, Dead Man's Plate, Sterak's Gage, Force of Nature, and Jak'Sho, swapping Mercury's Treads or Boots of Swiftness by game.
Add Randuin's Omen and Death's Dance as situational defense.
